proposal.refused:
Across the demonstrations, the goal was to reproduce the attached stick's ordered planar route around the tabletop obstacles. The failures occurred both at unsampled bypass turns and at gap arrivals, including repeated and final visits. The policy retained the entire ordered demonstration and correctly counted completed legs, but selected geometrically displaced endpoints: some bypasses extended several centimetres too far, and some gap targets stopped short or used an incorrectly identified tip feature. The reported failures therefore concern waypoint SUFFICIENCY in the application of the action instruction, not missing historical information or a demonstrated PREDICTABILITY failure in either memory field. No report establishes a NECESSITY violation.

I am not passing on the proposed additions of traversal-specific coordinates, frame associations, or worked feature identifications. The reported coordinates come from the recorded correct actions; merely placing them in the instructions would substitute episode answers for a generally observable localization rule. The reports do not supply independently verified distal-tip measurements that establish a new feature-identification method. In particular, projecting a recorded correct coordinate into an image does not independently establish which visible feature the policy should have selected.

The general changes requested by these reports are already explicit in the action instruction: identify the distal end-face centre rather than shaft, marker, or trail pixels; validate physical correspondence using the current calibrated TCP; fit incoming and outgoing segments with chronological observation assignments; constrain both planar coordinates; reject unsupported clearance extensions; distinguish approaching and departing samples from arrivals; pool repeated visits to a static gap without merging their chronological occurrences; reconstruct opposite-direction bypass turns separately; and corroborate the final tip against preceding arrival evidence. Repeating these rules or adding one clause per failed traversal would not resolve the reported measurement errors. Some reports loosely call nearby samples 'arrivals', while others correctly identify those same types of samples as still approaching or already departing; those labels should not override the existing requirement to establish their roles from the images.

Leave both memory fields and their update rules unchanged. The retained demonstration contains the supporting views requested in the reports, and the completed-leg transitions were correct throughout the reported failures. No additional memory fact or actionable, independently grounded replacement localization rule is established by this minibatch, so I am not proposing a change to any of the three texts.

fields.name: demonstration
fields.description: At the video cycle, record the ordered list of all supplied demonstration frame labels, including the initial and final frames. Preserve this list unchanged throughout execution. These images specify the entire demonstrated route, including obstacle sides, intermediate turns, reversals, repeated visits and the stopping point; do not replace it with an unordered set of visited places. e.g. ["V0", "V16", "V32", "V48", "V64", "V80", "V96", "V99"]
fields.annotation: At the video cycle, record the ordered list of all supplied demonstration frame labels, including the initial and final frames. Preserve this list unchanged throughout execution. These images specify the entire demonstrated route, including obstacle sides, intermediate turns, reversals, repeated visits and the stopping point; do not replace it with an unordered set of visited places. e.g. ["V0", "V16", "V32", "V48", "V64", "V80", "V96", "V99"]

fields.name: completed_legs
fields.description: Write zero at the video cycle and initial act cycle. At subsequent act cycles, use the incoming count to identify the next uncompleted endpoint in demonstration. Compare the current TCP and the observed motion with that endpoint. Increment by one only if the motion shown has reached it within 1 cm; otherwise preserve the count. Count bypass endpoints and repeated visits separately. An explicitly zero-step action, an incomplete approach or a wait does not advance the count. Record only arrivals already observed, never the endpoint of the action being selected now. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: The number of demonstrated waypoint-to-waypoint legs already completed by the execution at the current observation, excluding the action selected at this cycle. Set to zero at the video cycle and the initial act cycle. Increment when the observed execution reaches the next demonstrated leg endpoint within 1 cm. Count intermediate bypass points as endpoints, not just marked gaps. Repeated visits count separately in chronological order. Do not increment for a motion that executes no steps, an incomplete approach, or a wait. Preserve the count otherwise. e.g. 2

texts.action:
At the video cycle, produce memory only. At execution start, the stick is already at the demonstrated starting point: do not add a grasp, lift or approach action. Use demonstration to reconstruct the ordered planar route of the lower free end of the attached stick. Follow the actual stick tip, not the robot housing or the red marker: a red marker can remain at the previous gap while the tip travels around an obstacle. The white trail helps identify which side was traversed, but is not itself the complete task history.

Identify the ordered legs and assign demonstration frames to their incoming and outgoing segments, including bypasses beside obstacle ends and arrivals at gaps. Approximate 25-control-step boundaries are segmentation aids only: a nearby displayed frame need not show an endpoint, and elapsed time must not be converted into distance by assuming constant speed. Reconstruct unsampled endpoints geometrically as described below. Use the full video to distinguish retracing a bypass from continuing around the opposite end. Preserve all repetitions as separate chronological occurrences; reaching a previously visited gap does not mean the route is finished. Do not force bypass turns on opposite-direction traversals to share coordinates merely because they pass the same obstacle end. Do not assume that all obstacles must be visited or that every traversal alternates sides.

Identify the stick as the narrow rigid extension beneath the hand and track the centre of its distal end through the demonstration. Use the reported current TCP and front-camera calibration to check which physical feature represents the free tip at z=0.07 m. Compare its projection with the centre of the visible distal end face and the adjoining shaft boundaries, not merely the lowest bright or gray pixel. If the current wrist image shows the tool and its calibration is supplied, cross-check that same physical correspondence there. This validates the current feature identification, not an unseen historical wrist view. Track the corresponding distal end-face centre through demonstration frames using shaft continuity and geometry; do not transfer a constant image-space offset to other poses. Do not measure the lowest pixel of the hand, shaft centre, robot housing, marker, trail, or a silhouette edge below the end face. If the distal end face is occluded or cannot be distinguished reliably, treat its measurement as unavailable rather than assigning a precise coordinate to a substitute feature. Convert its pixel (u,v) into world coordinates using the camera calibration: C=-R^T t, d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1]^T, and X=C+((0.07-C_z)/d_z)d. Perform this ray-plane calculation rather than estimating metric offsets visually.

Before fitting an unsampled turn, assign each measurement to its chronological leg. Use the preceding arrival and samples strictly before the turn for the incoming segment, and samples strictly after the turn and the following arrival for the outgoing segment. Do not treat a departure sample as evidence of the preceding arrival. Fit the incoming and outgoing planar directions using multiple frames wherever available, preferentially using clear interior distal-tip measurements; downweight uncertain measurements and exclude occluded-tip substitutions. Fit both world x and y freely: an apparently axial image trajectory or vertical shaft does not justify preserving a current world coordinate. Extend both fitted segments to their intersection to recover the shared endpoint; with noisy observations, use a joint least-squares fit with a shared endpoint. Do not interpolate directly between the last incoming sample and first outgoing sample, which cuts across the corner. Those two samples alone do not determine two directions: use neighboring frames farther along each segment, clearly observed start or arrival positions, and obstacle geometry as additional constraints. For collinear reversals, where line intersection does not determine the endpoint, use observed arrival or repeated-visit evidence and gap geometry rather than inventing an intersection. Validate the shared endpoint as a joint measurement fit: project it and both fitted segments into every usable supporting demonstration image and inspect residuals against the identified distal end-face centres, respecting measurement uncertainty. Keep each supporting observation assigned to its preceding arrival, incoming interior, outgoing interior, or following arrival role throughout the check. Where physical-feature interpretations are ambiguous, compare candidate interpretations jointly across the adjoining traversal rather than choosing each frame's pixel independently. Accept the fit only when reliable incoming and outgoing observations support their respective segments in chronological order, the endpoint follows the last incoming observation and precedes the first outgoing observation along the route, and the demonstrated obstacle side is preserved. Reject an endpoint supported only by shaft or trail features, by extending only one fitted direction, by misassigned arrival/departure evidence, or by a rounded trail corner treated as a straight tip trajectory. Numerical reprojection consistency alone does not validate physical feature identity. If directions remain underconstrained, use adjoining arrival evidence and other demonstrated views of the same geometric location; do not invent a longer clearance move. When the tip is occluded, use neighboring visible tip positions, shaft and trail evidence, and obstacle geometry as supporting constraints; do not substitute shaft or trail pixels into the tip-height projection.

For a gap arrival, distinguish the full arrival from a sample still approaching the gap. Locate the endpoint from incoming and outgoing path evidence, refining it with the marked gap center only when the marker's own plane is established. Recover the marker's planar coordinates on that plane, then set the commanded TCP height to 0.07 m; never project a ground-marker pixel onto the tip-height plane. Gather arrival and departure evidence from all demonstrated visits to the same static gap to constrain its common location, including the retained starting view and any clear final visit. A still-approaching sample constrains the incoming segment, not the arrival position. Share the gap location without merging chronological occurrences: each visit consumes its own leg. Do not impose shared coordinates on bypass turns merely because they pass the same obstacle end. For the final endpoint, explicitly identify the distal-tip centre in the final demonstration frame and corroborate the feature identification with preceding arrival frames. Apply the calibrated z=0.07 m ray-plane calculation to that pixel and reproject the resulting coordinate to check numerical consistency; reprojection alone does not establish that the chosen feature is the tip. Discard any pixel/world-coordinate pair that disagrees under the calibration and resolve the measurement rather than accepting either as authoritative. If the final tip is occluded, use the existing occlusion and arrival-evidence rules, not a shaft or trail substitute. Do not extrapolate beyond the supported stopping point to a nominal gap coordinate or nominal leg length.
